I. GENERAL
As we have known together that the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, specifically Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this matter is as stated in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.
This matter is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, likewise acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects regarding domestic violence.
As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity.
Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that -17- Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases I acts of violence against women and children must I receive very serious handling and attention.
Related to this matter the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women And Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children as well as how to seek protection.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 4
The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance, and supervision, community participation and financing.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkayang Regency.
2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a child still in the womb.
8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: blind, deaf, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children.
9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect -5- children so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection I is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
17. Violence is any act that results or will result in suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
-6-
18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
21. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others.
23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
27. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved -7-.
28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
31. Accompaniment is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

2.3.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences discuss reporting and monitoring/reporting of activities and cases, but do not explicitly establish a dedicated data collection system or information system for VAW/women’s protection (e.g., a database, registry, or information management system).

I. GENERAL
As we have known together that the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, specifically Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this matter is as stated in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.
This matter is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, likewise acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects regarding domestic violence.
As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity.
Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that -17- Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases I acts of violence against women and children must I receive very serious handling and attention.
Related to this matter the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women And Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children as well as how to seek protection.

3.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text defines “Pengaduan” in Pasal 1 angka 22 as a written/oral notification to an authorized institution, and establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for protection/services (Pasal 1 angka 24–25; Pasal 8–11). It also mandates community reporting (“melaporkan adanya kekerasan”) in Pasal 17 and Pasal 23. While no ‘hotline number’ is specified, the regulation clearly provides for complaint/report intake mechanisms via authorized institutions/P2TP2A. Given the golden label is “Yes,” and the text supports the existence of reporting/complaint channels (even if not a hotline), the golden label aligns with the document and the judge’s ‘No’ seems incorrect.

4.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly assigns educational institutions a role in carrying out prevention efforts, indicating prevention through the education sector.

Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
21. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others.
23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
27. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved -7-.
28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
31. Accompaniment is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 4
The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance, and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 19
(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.
(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

6.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text provides explicit protections for victims/witnesses involved in legal processes. Pasal 5 ayat (1) huruf a grants protection from threats related to testimony, and huruf g grants “pendampingan pada setiap tingkatan pemeriksaan dan selama proses peradilan dan proses di luar pengadilan” (assistance at every level of examination and during judicial and out-of-court processes). This directly addresses involvement in legal processes. The judge’s Yes is correct based on the regulation, so the golden label “No” appears incorrect.
